about: The weekly puzzle, one a week in this order from Monday 30 November 2026 (see src/app/community.js and .github/workflows/weekly-puzzle.yml). Each answer is a single number. Add new puzzles at the end so past weeks keep their numbers.

puzzles.hook: Two taps and a leak. Does the tank ever fill?
puzzles.question: Tap A fills a tank in 6 hours and tap B in 3 hours. A leak empties a full tank in 4 hours. With both taps and the leak open on an empty tank, how many hours until it is full?
puzzles.hint: Think in 'tank per hour': add what the taps put in and subtract what the leak takes out.
method: In one hour: A fills 1/6, B fills 1/3, the leak empties 1/4.
So the tank is full in 4 hours.

puzzles.hook: Mark up 25%, discount 20%. Who wins: the shop or you?
puzzles.question: A shopkeeper marks an item 25% above its cost price, then gives a 20% discount on the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
puzzles.hint: Take the cost as 100 and follow the price through both changes.
method: Cost 100, so the marked price is 125.
A 20% discount on 125 is 25, so the selling price is 100.
Selling price equals cost: 0% profit. A 25% rise is undone by a 20% fall, because 1.25 × 0.8 = 1.

puzzles.hook: 30 km/h there, 60 km/h back. The average is not 45.
puzzles.question: You drive to a town at 30 km/h and come back the same way at 60 km/h. What is your average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
puzzles.hint: Average speed is total distance over total time. Pick a convenient distance, like 60 km each way.
method: Say the town is 60 km away.
Going takes 60/30 = 2 hours; coming back takes 60/60 = 1 hour.
Total: 120 km in 3 hours, so 40 km/h. (Shortcut for equal distances: 2ab/(a+b) = 2·30·60/90 = 40.)

puzzles.hook: Two trains, head on. How long until they are past each other?
puzzles.question: A 120 m train at 50 km/h and a 180 m train at 40 km/h run towards each other on parallel tracks. How many seconds do they take to cross each other completely?
puzzles.hint: Moving towards each other, their speeds add. The distance to cover is both lengths together.

puzzles.hook: Petrol goes up 25%. Your budget does not. Cut by how much?
puzzles.question: The price of petrol rises by 25%. By what percentage must you reduce how much you use, so that you spend exactly the same as before?
puzzles.hint: Spending = price × quantity. The new quantity must bring the product back to where it was.
method: To keep spending at 100, quantity must fall to 100/125 = 0.8 of what it was.
That is a 20% cut. In general a rise of r% needs a cut of r/(100 + r) × 100%.

puzzles.hook: At 3:40 the hands look close. They are not.
puzzles.question: What is the angle, in degrees, between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40?
puzzles.hint: The hour hand does not wait at 3: it moves half a degree every minute.

puzzles.hook: Three bells ring together at 9:00. When is the next time?
puzzles.question: Three bells ring every 6, 8 and 12 minutes. They ring together at 9:00. After how many minutes do they next ring together?
puzzles.hint: You need a number of minutes that each of 6, 8 and 12 divides.
method: So they ring together again after 24 minutes, at 9:24.

puzzles.hook: Three times as old now, twice as old later. How old is the son?
puzzles.question: A father is three times as old as his son. In 12 years he will be twice as old as his son. How old is the son now?
puzzles.hint: Both of them get 12 years older. Write the 'in 12 years' sentence as an equation.

puzzles.hook: Ten people, everyone shakes everyone's hand once. How many handshakes?
puzzles.question: At a meeting of 10 people, each person shakes hands exactly once with every other person. How many handshakes are there?
puzzles.hint: A handshake is a pair of people. How many pairs can you choose from 10?
method: Each handshake is a choice of 2 people out of 10.
(Counting 10 × 9 = 90 counts each handshake twice, once from each side.)

puzzles.hook: A takes 10 days, B takes 15. Together: not 12.5.
puzzles.question: A can finish a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, in how many days do they finish it?
puzzles.hint: Add their work per day, not their days.
method: A does 1/10 of the job a day, B does 1/15.

puzzles.hook: Downstream in 2 hours, back up in 3. How fast is the river?
puzzles.question: A boat goes 24 km downstream in 2 hours and the same 24 km upstream in 3 hours. What is the speed of the stream, in km/h?
puzzles.hint: Downstream speed = boat + stream; upstream speed = boat − stream.
method: (And the boat in still water: (12 + 8)/2 = 10 km/h.)

puzzles.hook: 100! is a 158-digit number. How many zeros does it end with?
puzzles.question: How many zeros are at the end of 100! (that is, 1 × 2 × 3 × … × 100)?
puzzles.hint: Each trailing zero needs a 10 = 2 × 5. There are plenty of 2s: count the 5s.
method: Multiples of 25 give an extra 5 each: 100/25 = 4.

puzzles.hook: Five friends, one round table. How many different seatings?
puzzles.question: In how many different ways can 5 people sit around a round table, if only who sits next to whom matters (rotations of the same seating count once)?
puzzles.hint: Seat one person anywhere: around a circle that fixes the rotation. Then arrange the rest.
method: Fix one person's seat to remove rotations.
The other 4 can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways.
In general, n people around a table: (n − 1)! ways.

puzzles.hook: Same money, same rate, same time. Why does compound interest pay more?
puzzles.question: On ₹10,000 at 10% a year for 2 years, how many rupees more does compound interest (compounded yearly) give than simple interest?
puzzles.hint: In year 2, compound interest also earns interest on year 1's interest.
method: Difference ₹100: year 1's ₹1,000 interest earning 10% in year 2. (Shortcut: P × (r/100)² = 10,000 × 0.01.)

puzzles.hook: Make salty water weaker without removing any salt.
puzzles.question: How many litres of water must be added to 30 litres of a 20% salt solution to make it a 15% solution?
puzzles.hint: Adding water does not change the amount of salt.
method: For 6 litres to be 15% of the mixture, the mixture must be 6 / 0.15 = 40 litres.

puzzles.hook: 7 to the power 2026 has 1,713 digits. You only need the last one.
puzzles.question: What is the last (units) digit of 7^2026?
puzzles.hint: Write out the last digits of 7, 7², 7³, 7⁴, 7⁵… and look for a cycle.
method: Last digits of powers of 7 repeat: 7, 9, 3, 1, 7, 9, 3, 1, …
So 7^2026 ends like 7², which ends in 9.
